L1-S01.title: The Night the Lights Blew Away

titleCard.text: Episode 1. The Night the Lights Blew Away.

scenes.setting: Lantern Hill at night: a small town of colourful houses climbing a hill, the sea at the bottom. At the top, the Lantern Clock, its twelve round lights glowing.
scenes.action: Slow camera up the hill. Wind rises; clouds roll in. The twelve lights wobble, pop off and fly away over the roofs like fireflies.

lines.text: This is Lantern Hill. At the very top is the Lantern Clock. It has twelve lights.
One night, a big wind came. Whooosh!
And all twelve lights blew away!

scenes.setting: Morning. Nana Lucía’s workshop: shelves of jars full of bolts, a big wooden table, sun through the window.
scenes.action: Amara runs in with a newspaper. Spark hovers, worried. Bolt chases his own antenna tail.

lines.text: Nana! The clock has no lights! And the Night of a Hundred Lights is coming soon!
Twelve lights, lost all over town. We have to find them!
Beep-woof!
Then we need one more helper.

scenes.setting: Same workshop. A dusty box on a high shelf, tied with string. The label says: FOR A NEW HELPER.
scenes.action: Nana Lucía lifts the box down and blows off the dust. She turns to the camera — to the child.

lines.text: When I was young, I built robots. I kept this box for someone new.
Someone just like you.
A robot kit! You can build your very own robot!

scenes.setting: Workshop table. A toaster, a toy car and Bolt sit in a row.
scenes.action: Spark points at each one in turn. A ball rolls past Bolt: Bolt’s ears twitch (a glow on his ears), a thought bubble shows a ball, then he runs after it.

lines.text: Is a toaster a robot? Hmm. It cannot see you. It cannot decide anything.
Is a toy car a robot? Not if you push it. It does what your hand does.
Watch Bolt. He sees the ball. He thinks, "Ball!" And he runs!
Sense. Think. Act. That is what a robot does!
Can you say it with me? Sense! Think! Act!
lines.direction: Pause for the children to answer.

scenes.setting: The kit is open on the table: four different robot bodies in a row.
scenes.action: Spark taps each body. Inside each one we glimpse a small battery and a tiny computer “brain”.

lines.text: Every robot needs a body. It keeps the battery and the brain safe inside.
The battery gives it energy. The brain is a tiny computer that follows the plan.
Pick the body you like best!

scenes.setting: The child’s new robot body on the table. Its eyes light up for the first time.
scenes.action: The robot blinks. It does nothing else. Spark leans in, puzzled.

lines.text: Hello? Hello, robot?
A robot only does what its program tells it. A program is a list of steps.
Let’s teach it to say hello.
Beep! Hello!

scenes.setting: Workshop floor near the door. Evening light.
scenes.action: Bolt sniffs under the door. A soft golden glow slips past outside — one of the clock lights, rolling away down the path.

lines.text: Beep-woof? Beep-woof!
A clock light! Right outside! But… our robot has no wheels yet!

cliffhanger.text: A clock light rolls past the door — and the new robot cannot move yet. Next time: wheels!

previously.text: The clock lights blew away. You built your robot’s body. A light rolled past the door…

scenes.setting: Workshop table. The robot body from last time.
scenes.action: Spark lays out two wheels, two small motors and a little ball wheel.

lines.text: That light is rolling away! Let’s give your robot wheels!
Each wheel has a motor. A motor is a little spinner.
Energy from the battery makes it spin. The spin turns the wheel.

scenes.setting: Close-up under the robot.
scenes.action: X-ray view: battery glows, a line of light runs to each motor, motors spin, wheels turn. Then the little ball at the back rolls freely.

lines.text: Only two wheels? Won’t it fall over?
See this little ball at the back? It rolls any way. It holds the robot up.
Two wheels to push, one ball to balance!

scenes.setting: The workshop doorstep, then the garden path outside, lined with flowerpots.
scenes.action: The robot rolls out of the door for the first time. It goes too far and stops in the grass. Bolt laughs (beep-woof!).

lines.text: Wheee!
Too far! The robot does not know where the light is. We must tell it how far to go.
Look — the path has squares. Let’s count them. One, two, three!
How many squares to the light? Count with me!
lines.direction: Pause for the children to count.

scenes.setting: Garden path. A golden clock light glows beside a flowerpot.
scenes.action: The robot hops exactly to the light and stops. The light jumps happily onto the robot’s back. Counter on screen: 1 of 12.

lines.text: You found the first light! One!
Good counting makes good robots.

scenes.setting: The light on the robot’s back starts to flicker and points like a compass down the hill.
scenes.action: An arrow of light points at the bakery at the bottom of the street.

lines.text: It’s pointing! Another light must be near Mr Okafor’s bakery!
Beep-woof! Sniff sniff… bread!

cliffhanger.text: The first light points the way down the hill — to the busiest street in town.

previously.text: Your robot got wheels and found the first light. The light pointed to the bakery…

scenes.setting: Bakery Lane: a busy street going down the hill. Mr Okafor’s bakery, warm smells drawn as swirls.
scenes.action: The team follows the light’s arrow. A bread cart rolls across the street.

lines.text: The light points into the bakery! Let’s go!
Careful, little ones! My bread cart crosses here every morning!

scenes.setting: Bakery Lane. The robot rolls towards the cart’s path.
scenes.action: The robot rolls straight on. Just in time the cart stops. Crumbs fly; nobody is hurt; a loaf lands on Bolt’s head.

lines.text: Stop! The robot didn’t wait!
Beep-woof?
lines.direction: Wearing a loaf like a hat.

lines.text: Our robot does every step right away. It needs a step that says: wait.

scenes.setting: Kerb at the side of the street.
scenes.action: Spark draws three cards in the air: GO, WAIT, GO. Then shuffles them: GO, GO, WAIT — and the cartoon robot bumps the cart.

lines.text: Go one. Wait. Then go again!
What if we mix the cards up? Go, go, then wait?
Then it waits AFTER the crash. The order is important!
Which card comes first? You choose!

scenes.setting: Bakery Lane, second try.
scenes.action: Robot hops once, waits as the cart rolls by, then hops to the bakery door. Mr Okafor claps with floury hands.

lines.text: What a polite robot!
Beep! Good morning!

scenes.setting: Inside the bakery. Shelves of bread from around the world: flatbread, round loaves, buns.
scenes.action: The clock light glows from inside a tall stack of bread baskets. People bustle everywhere. A small girl hides behind her dad’s leg, afraid of the robot.

lines.text: There’s the light! But the bakery is so busy…
And that little girl looks scared of our robot.

cliffhanger.text: The second light is inside the crowded bakery — and a little girl is frightened of the robot. How can people know what a robot will do?

previously.text: The robot learned to wait. The second light was hidden in the busy bakery…

scenes.setting: Inside the busy bakery.
scenes.action: The robot rolls in. People step back. The small girl, Noor, hides behind her dad.

lines.text: Is it going to bump me?
She can’t tell what our robot will do next.

scenes.setting: Bakery corner. Nana Lucía crouches next to Noor.
scenes.action: Nana pulls a small round screen from her bag. On it, two friendly eyes blink.

lines.text: When you cross the road, the driver waves. You know they saw you.
A robot can show a face and tell people what it will do.
A face screen!

scenes.setting: The robot with its new face screen.
scenes.action: The screen shows an arrow and a smile. The robot speaks before it moves.

lines.text: Hello! I am going forward now.
Oh! It told me! Hello, robot!
When people know what a robot will do, they feel safe.
What would YOUR robot say before it moves?

scenes.setting: Bread basket stack. The clock light glows inside.
scenes.action: The robot says "Excuse me!", rolls to the baskets, beeps. The light floats out and lands on its back. Counter: 2 of 12.

lines.text: Excuse me! Found a light!
Two lights! Ten more to go!

scenes.setting: Outside the bakery. The town square below, with a round fountain.
scenes.action: The second light points down to the fountain. But the path to it bends around a corner.

lines.text: The next light is by the fountain. But the street turns a corner!
Beep-woof?
Our robot only goes straight. How will it turn?

cliffhanger.text: The next light is around a corner, and the robot only knows how to go straight. How do robots turn?

previously.text: Your robot got a face. The second light was in the bread baskets. The next light was near the fountain…

scenes.setting: The town square of Lantern Hill: a round fountain in the middle, benches, pigeons, a fruit stall.
scenes.action: The robot faces a corner. It hops forward and bumps gently into a bench.

lines.text: Oops! Straight is not always the way.
We need to turn. But how does a robot turn?

scenes.setting: Close-up under the robot, X-ray view.
scenes.action: Left wheel spins backwards, right wheel spins forwards: the robot spins on the spot like a dancer. Then the other way.

lines.text: Watch the wheels. One goes forward. One goes back.
The robot spins right on the spot!
Like when you push one side of a roundabout and pull the other!

scenes.setting: The square. The robot faces the camera; Amara stands behind it.
scenes.action: Amara holds up her right hand. The robot turns — to ITS right, which looks like left to us. Bolt tilts his head.

lines.text: Turn right! Wait… it went the other way?
It turned to ITS right. Pretend you are sitting inside the robot.
Stand up and turn like your robot. Turn right! Now turn left!
lines.direction: Pause for children to stand and turn.

scenes.setting: The square, seen from above. Squares drawn on the stones; the fountain in the middle.
scenes.action: The robot goes up, turns right, goes along the top. A sparkle near the fountain wall: the light! It jumps up — and lands IN the fountain bowl.

lines.text: Turning right!
There it is! Oh no, it jumped into the fountain!

scenes.setting: The fountain. Townspeople gather, looking sad: the festival decorations are not ready.
scenes.action: The light glows at the bottom of the fountain bowl, out of reach. Nana Lucía has an idea and smiles.

lines.text: Everyone looks sad. A happy dance might shake the fountain — and cheer up the town.
A robot dance! Can our robot dance?

cliffhanger.text: The third light is stuck in the fountain. Nana has an idea: a robot dance! But what kind of dance will YOUR robot do?

L1-S06.sessionTitle: Make It Yours: My Robot’s Dance
L1-S06.title: The Dance That Shook the Fountain

titleCard.text: Episode 6. The Dance That Shook the Fountain.

previously.text: Your robot learned to turn. The third light jumped into the fountain…

scenes.setting: The town square at noon. A small crowd. The light glows in the fountain bowl.
scenes.action: Nana Lucía hands the child a sketch pad. Spark draws a robot with arrows around it.

lines.text: Every great machine starts as a drawing. First plan, then build.
Your robot needs a name, colours… and a dance!

scenes.setting: Amara’s sketch: arrows, turn signs and music notes.
scenes.action: Amara shows her plan: forward, spin, beep, back. She tests it with Spark — Spark bumps the bench, they laugh, and she changes one arrow.

lines.text: My first plan bumped the bench. So I changed one step.
That is what engineers do. Try. Look. Fix. Try again.

scenes.setting: The square, the robot centre stage.
scenes.action: Montage of possible dances: spins, hops, beeps, songs. The crowd claps. The fountain water wobbles with the rhythm.

lines.text: Now it’s your turn. Make your robot’s dance!

scenes.setting: The square after the dance (this scene plays after the child shares).
scenes.action: The water splashes; the light pops out of the fountain and lands on the robot. Counter: 3 of 12. The crowd cheers. A grey cloud drifts over the map pinned to the town notice board.

lines.text: Bravo, little robot!
Three lights! And look — Nana’s old town map! It shows every street.
Beep-woof!
lines.direction: Grabs the map and runs off, playing.

lines.text: Bolt! Come back with that map!

cliffhanger.text: Three lights found! But Bolt has run off with Nana’s map of the whole town…

previously.text: Three lights found. Bolt ran off with Nana’s map…

scenes.setting: Lantern Hill market: stripy stalls of fruit, cloth, pots and spices; narrow lanes between them.
scenes.action: Bolt dashes between stalls with the map in his mouth. The team chases him and loses him in the lanes.

lines.text: Bolt! Where did he go?
These lanes are like a maze!

scenes.setting: Ms Mei’s fruit stall. Bolt sits proudly, the map at his feet, a mango on his head.
scenes.action: Ms Mei waves from the far corner of the market.

lines.text: Your puppy is here! Come round the back of the cloth stall!
If we just go, we’ll get lost. Let’s plan the whole way first.

scenes.setting: Spark projects a glowing grid map of the market in the air.
scenes.action: Amara puts arrow stickers on the map: turn, go 2, turn, go 3. Spark traces it with a dotted line.

lines.text: A plan with steps in order has a special name. An algorithm.
Al-go-rith-m! Like a recipe — but for robots.
Straight bits and turns. Straight, turn, straight!
Can you find the turns on the map? Point to them!

scenes.setting: The market lanes.
scenes.action: The robot follows the plan exactly and arrives at the fruit stall. Bolt licks the robot. Ms Mei gives Bolt a pat and hands back the map.

lines.text: Plan done! Hello, Bolt!
Beep-woof…

scenes.setting: Ms Mei’s stall. The map lies open; Nana’s old handwritten program cards are tucked inside it, now muddled.
scenes.action: The fourth light glows among the flower buckets of the stall next door. Bolt sneezes and the program cards scatter into a jumble.

lines.text: The fourth light — in the flower stall! I wrote a plan to get there…
But Bolt sneezed and mixed up the cards!

cliffhanger.text: The plan to reach the fourth light got mixed up. Is it still right? Something is wrong — but what?

previously.text: The robot planned a path through the market. Bolt sneezed and mixed up the program…

scenes.setting: Ms Mei’s stall. Spark gathers the jumbled program cards.
scenes.action: Spark puts the cards back in order — or thinks so — and the robot runs them. It turns the wrong way and rolls towards the pot stall.

lines.text: All fixed! Go, robot!
Stop! It’s going the wrong way!
Oops!
lines.direction: Face screen shows a wobbly mouth.

scenes.setting: Nana Lucía sits on a crate with a cup of tea.
scenes.action: She tells a story. A little picture shows an old room-sized computer and a small moth.

lines.text: Engineers have called mistakes "bugs" for a very long time. Once, they found a REAL moth stuck in a giant computer!
They taped it in their notebook as "the first real bug" — a joke! Any mistake in a program is a bug. Every engineer makes them. Me too!
So a bug is not bad. It’s a puzzle!

scenes.setting: The cards laid out next to the map.
scenes.action: Spark becomes a detective with a magnifying glass. The robot replays its run in slow motion; at the wrong turn, a big question mark pops up.

lines.text: Watch the robot. Where did it stop doing what we planned?
There! It turned right, but our arrow says left!
Found the bug! Change just that one card.
Did you see it too? Point when the robot goes wrong!

scenes.setting: The flower stall: buckets of sunflowers, marigolds and roses.
scenes.action: Fixed program. The robot rolls to the flowers and stops. The fourth light rises from a bucket of marigolds. Counter: 4 of 12.

lines.text: Found a light!
So THAT’S why my marigolds were glowing!

scenes.setting: A puddle by the fountain. Bolt splashes in it with the map.
scenes.action: The map is soaked. The ink of the path to the school runs and fades away.

lines.text: Bolt! The path to the school is all washed away!
How will we find our way now?

cliffhanger.text: Four lights! But Bolt splashed the map, and the path to the school has washed away. Could the robot draw a new one?

previously.text: Four lights. The map got wet and the path to the school washed away…

scenes.setting: The fountain square. The wet map is drying on a bench.
scenes.action: The path to the school has faded. Amara looks sad. Spark hovers over the map.

lines.text: We can’t find the school without the path.
What if the robot drew a new path as it goes?

scenes.setting: Nana Lucía’s workshop. A drawer full of tools.
scenes.action: Nana pulls out a pen holder that clips under a robot.

lines.text: A robot can hold a pen. Pen down — it draws. Pen up — it stops drawing.
Then we can see exactly where it went.
A robot artist!

scenes.setting: A long roll of paper laid on the street to the school.
scenes.action: The robot puts its pen down and rolls forward: a straight line appears. It turns — and the line bends. Bolt follows the line, sniffing.

lines.text: Pen down! Drawing!
Look, it draws a line everywhere it goes!
If you forget "pen up", what will happen?
It keeps drawing — everywhere!
lines.direction: Cartoon: the robot scribbles all over the street; Bolt is covered in lines.

scenes.setting: A zebra crossing on the way to school. Cars wait; the lollipop lady holds up her sign.
scenes.action: The robot reaches the crossing. Spark holds up a paw-like hand: stop! The robot lifts its pen, crosses with everyone, and puts the pen down again on the far side.

lines.text: We don’t draw on the road! Pen up to cross.
Pen up… crossing… pen down!
Now there’s a gap in the line, right where the road is!

scenes.setting: The school gate: a cheerful building with a playground.
scenes.action: The drawn path leads right to the gate. Teacher Ms Adaeze waves. Behind her the playground is half-ready for the festival games.

lines.text: Welcome! We need help drawing the game squares for the festival.
A square… that’s a lot of drawing!

cliffhanger.text: The school needs game squares drawn for the festival — lots of them. Is there a faster way than block, block, block?

previously.text: The robot got a pen and drew the way to school. The school needed game squares…

scenes.setting: The school playground. Children waiting with chalk-less hands.
scenes.action: The robot draws a square, block by block. It takes ages. Bolt falls asleep, snoring "beep-zzz".

lines.text: Forward. Turn. Forward. Turn. Forward. Turn. Forward. Turn.
That’s eight blocks for one square! We need twenty squares!

scenes.setting: Close on the eight blocks.
scenes.action: Spark colours the blocks in pairs: forward+turn is blue, then blue, blue, blue.

lines.text: Look! Forward, turn. Forward, turn. The same two steps, four times!
When something happens again and again, we use a Repeat block.
Put the steps inside, and say how many times.

scenes.setting: Ms Adaeze leads the class in a clapping song.
scenes.action: Clap-clap-stomp, clap-clap-stomp, clap-clap-stomp. The children do it with her.

lines.text: Our songs repeat too! Clap, clap, stomp — three times!
Can you do it with them? Clap, clap, stomp!
lines.direction: Pause for the class to join in.

scenes.setting: Playground.
scenes.action: With Repeat 4, the robot zooms round a square in one go. Square after square appears. The children cheer and play.

lines.text: Repeat four times! Done!
Three blocks instead of eight!

scenes.setting: Under the playground slide.
scenes.action: A child playing in the new square sees a glow under the slide: the fifth light! Counter: 5 of 12. Then a gust of wind blows a library poster across the playground: "The library is closed — the steps are broken."

lines.text: Five lights! But what about the library?
The library steps need new markings. They go up, and up, and up…

cliffhanger.text: Five lights! The library steps need new lines — step after step after step. Is there a pattern?

previously.text: Five lights. The robot learned Repeat and drew squares at the school…

scenes.setting: The Lantern Hill library: an old building with a long staircase up to its door. The painted step lines have worn away.
scenes.action: Mr Haruto the librarian stands at the top holding a stack of books.

lines.text: Nobody can see the edges of the steps. People trip!
Our robot can draw new lines on the step plan!

scenes.setting: Inside the library: books open on a table showing patterns.
scenes.action: Pages show a rangoli of coloured powder, a strip of kente cloth, blue mosaic tiles and a woven basket. Spark circles the part that repeats on each one.

lines.text: People all over the world make patterns. A pattern is a part that repeats.
This cloth goes stripe, zig-zag, stripe, zig-zag!
Find the piece that repeats. Then you only need to say it once — and Repeat!

scenes.setting: The step plan spread out on the library floor.
scenes.action: Spark draws one step: up, turn, along, turn. Then it glows and copies itself: step, step, step.

lines.text: One step is: up, turn right, along, turn left.
How many steps are there? Count with me!
lines.direction: Pause; the stairs show three steps.

lines.text: Three! So, Repeat 3!

scenes.setting: The library staircase, freshly marked.
scenes.action: The robot finishes the drawing. Mr Haruto walks down safely and gives a thumbs up. He hands Amara a rolled-up blank festival banner.

lines.text: Thank you! Now — the festival banner is still empty. Could your robot help?
I can draw!

scenes.setting: Amara unrolls the banner a little. Something inside glows faintly.
scenes.action: She rolls it back up quickly to keep the surprise.

lines.text: Something is glowing inside the banner!
We will find out — when we draw on it!

cliffhanger.text: A blank banner — and something glowing rolled up inside it. What will YOU draw?

L1-S12.sessionTitle: Make It Yours: The Festival Banner
L1-S12.title: The Banner Surprise

previously.text: The robot drew the library steps. The empty banner had a glow inside…

scenes.setting: The town hall steps. The long blank banner is rolled out.
scenes.action: Townspeople gather. Ms Mei, Mr Okafor, Mr Haruto and Ms Adaeze each paint something small on the edge.

lines.text: Every festival banner shows what the town loves.
Then everyone should draw something. Even robots!

scenes.setting: Amara’s planning sheet: a house made of squares, a window that repeats.
scenes.action: Amara tests her house. The roof goes wrong; she fixes a turn. Spark claps.

lines.text: My house uses Repeat for the windows!
What will YOU draw? A house? A flower of squares? Steps up a mountain?

scenes.setting: The banner, after the children’s drawings (plays after sharing).
scenes.action: As the last line is drawn, the banner glows. The sixth light rolls out of the core of the banner. Counter: 6 of 12 — half! The six lights rise and point together, down the hill, to the harbour.

lines.text: Six lights! Halfway there!
They all point to the harbour. The rest must be down by the sea.
The harbour has heavy boxes, slippery docks and a dark tunnel…
Beep… woof?

cliffhanger.text: Halfway! Six lights point to the harbour — heavy boxes, slippery docks and a dark old tunnel.

previously.text: Halfway! Six lights pointed to the harbour…

scenes.setting: Lantern Hill harbour: wooden docks, colourful boats, gulls, nets drying in the sun.
scenes.action: The team arrives following the six lights. Captain Ingrid, the harbour master, is tangled up in a fishing net full of glass floats.

lines.text: The storm filled my nets with floats! And one of them is glowing!
A clock light, hiding with the floats!

scenes.setting: The dock. The robot tries to push a float with its pen — the float rolls away and plops into a bucket of water.
scenes.action: Bolt shakes off a splash.

lines.text: A pen can’t carry things. We need a different tool.
Engineers choose the tool for the job. A pen for drawing. For carrying… a scoop!

scenes.setting: Nana’s toolbox, opened on the dock.
scenes.action: Close-up: the pen clicks off; the scoop clicks on. The scoop tips up to hold, tips down to let go.

lines.text: Scoop up — it holds. Tip out — it lets go.
What else could a robot scoop? Sand? Rice? Toys?

scenes.setting: The dock with a row of floats and Captain Ingrid’s basket.
scenes.action: The robot rolls up, scoops a float, carries it, and tips it into the basket. The captain cheers. The glowing float is not among these — it rolled further, down the slipway.

lines.text: Scoop up! Tip out!
Splendid! But the glowing one rolled down to the old slipway.

scenes.setting: The bottom of the slipway: a steep ramp up from the water.
scenes.action: At the bottom sits a big iron lantern — the glowing float stuck inside it. It looks very heavy.

lines.text: It’s inside that big iron lantern. That looks SO heavy.
And it has to go UP the ramp…

cliffhanger.text: The seventh light is stuck inside a heavy iron lantern at the bottom of a steep ramp. Can a small robot carry something heavy uphill?

previously.text: The robot got a scoop and carried floats. The seventh light was inside a heavy iron lantern…

scenes.setting: Bottom of the slipway. The iron lantern with the glowing float inside.
scenes.action: The robot scoops the iron lantern. Its wheels strain. It hops up the ramp — and stops halfway, slowly.

lines.text: Hop 3… ugh… only got this far.
Yesterday Hop 3 went all the way. What changed?

scenes.setting: Nana sits on the ramp with Bolt on her lap.
scenes.action: Nana pushes an empty pram up the ramp easily, then a pram full of shopping bags — slowly, puffing.

lines.text: Pushing something heavy uphill is hard work. You go slower.
The hill pulls everything back down. The heavier it is, the more it pulls.
Our Hop block drives for the same time. But slower… means less far!

scenes.setting: A chalkboard on the dock. Three pictures: flat + empty, ramp + empty, ramp + heavy.
scenes.action: Spark asks the audience to guess. Then the robot tests each one; a mark shows where it stops each time.

lines.text: Which one goes the least far? Guess!
Up the ramp with the heavy lantern! That’s our problem.
So we test, and add a hop!

scenes.setting: Top of the ramp, the lighthouse platform.
scenes.action: With one more hop, the robot reaches the top. It tips out the lantern; the glowing float pops out — light 7! Counter: 7 of 12. Captain Ingrid opens the iron lantern for good.

lines.text: Made it! Found a light!
Seven! Next: the fish market. Mind the floor — it’s icy from the cold store!

scenes.setting: The fish market door slides open: a shiny wet floor, and past it, the sandy beach.
scenes.action: Bolt runs in and slides across the floor on his tummy — wheee — and lands in a heap.

lines.text: Beep-woooooof!
Slippery! Will our robot slide too?

cliffhanger.text: The next way goes over an icy floor and soft sand. Will the same program still work?

previously.text: The robot carried the heavy iron lantern up the ramp. Seven lights! Then Bolt slid across an icy floor…

scenes.setting: The fish market: a cold store has leaked, and a patch of the floor is frozen and shiny. Past the door, soft beach sand.
scenes.action: The robot hops onto the ice. It stops its wheels — but keeps sliding, spinning slowly, and bumps a stack of empty boxes.

lines.text: Stop! I said stop! Wheee!
The wheels stopped, but the robot kept going!

scenes.setting: Nana walks onto the ice in tiny, careful steps, arms out.
scenes.action: Then she steps onto the mat at the edge and walks normally.

lines.text: On ice, nothing holds your feet. Wheels can’t grip either.
So go slowly. Slow things slide less.

scenes.setting: The beach outside. The robot drives onto the sand.
scenes.action: The wheels sink a little and churn. The robot stops early, half-way to the mark.

lines.text: Now the opposite! Sand is soft. The wheels sink in and it is hard to roll.
Ice — too slippy. Sand — too sticky!
What will happen on ice? On sand? Show me with your hands!

scenes.setting: Fish market and beach together.
scenes.action: The robot creeps slowly over the ice, then pushes with an extra hop through the sand. It reaches the far side.

lines.text: Slow on ice… extra push in sand… made it!
Same robot, different floors, different plan!

scenes.setting: The far side of the beach: the lift bridge over the harbour channel, raised high. A ship’s horn sounds.
scenes.action: Across the bridge, at the foot of the lighthouse, something glows.

lines.text: The eighth light is across the bridge — but the bridge is up!
Beep-woof?
lines.direction: Looks up at the raised bridge.

cliffhanger.text: The eighth light is across the harbour bridge — and the bridge keeps going up and down for ships. When is it safe to cross?

previously.text: The robot crossed ice and sand. The eighth light was across the lift bridge…

scenes.setting: The lift bridge over the harbour channel. A ship toots and sails through as the bridge rises.
scenes.action: The bridge goes up, a boat passes, the bridge comes down, cars cross, then up again. A big clock on the bridge tower ticks.

lines.text: The bridge goes up for boats and down for people. Up, down, up, down!
Like a breathing bridge!

scenes.setting: At the stop line before the bridge.
scenes.action: Spark counts with the bridge clock: “It comes down… now! And stays down for a while.”

lines.text: Let’s count together. The bridge comes down after 1… 2… 3… 4!
Our robot can’t see the bridge. It has no eyes for that.
So we count for it. Go to the line, wait, then cross.

scenes.setting: The bridge, down.
scenes.action: The robot waits at the stop line, its face showing a little timer. The bridge lands. The robot crosses.

lines.text: Waiting… waiting… crossing now!
Good waiting!

scenes.setting: The foot of the lighthouse.
scenes.action: The robot finds the eighth light among the rocks. Counter: 8 of 12. Amara frowns at the bridge.

lines.text: Eight lights! But… what if the bridge changes its timing? Our count would be wrong.
Then one day your robot will need senses, to notice things for itself.

scenes.setting: The old railway tunnel entrance in the hillside behind the lighthouse. Pitch black inside.
scenes.action: The eight lights all point into the tunnel. Spark peeks in — her camera eyes see only darkness.

lines.text: The lights point into the old tunnel. But I can’t see a thing in there!
Beep… woof…

cliffhanger.text: The lights point into a pitch-dark tunnel. Spark’s camera eyes can’t see in the dark. What does a robot need in the dark?

previously.text: The robot waited for the bridges. Eight lights! They pointed into a dark tunnel…

scenes.setting: The tunnel mouth. Inside: pure darkness.
scenes.action: Spark flies in a little and immediately bumps the wall — “ow!” — and flies back out.

lines.text: My camera eyes see nothing! Cameras need light, just like your eyes.
And in the dark, nobody could see our robot coming.

scenes.setting: Nana Lucía holds up a torch, switching it on and off.
scenes.action: Off: black. On: the beam hits a wall and the wall appears. Little arrows show light bouncing from the wall into Spark’s eye.

lines.text: Light shines out, bounces off things and comes back into eyes and cameras. That is how we see.
A light uses battery energy. So we switch it on in the dark, and off in the light.

scenes.setting: Toolbox on the dock.
scenes.action: The scoop clicks off; the headlight clicks on.

lines.text: Scoop off. Headlight on! A new tool for a new job.
When should we switch the light on? Before the tunnel or after?

scenes.setting: Inside the tunnel, lit by the robot’s headlight.
scenes.action: The beam shows old rails, puddles and, on the ceiling, tiny blue glow-worms. Spark gasps. They walk through together.

lines.text: Light on!
Glow-worms! Like the caves in New Zealand!
Now I can see — and everyone can see us!

scenes.setting: The far end of the tunnel opens near the top of the hill, by Nana’s little house. Thick white fog everywhere.
scenes.action: The robot switches its light off at the exit. Fog swallows the path. Somewhere, a light glows faintly — inside Nana’s house.

lines.text: Light off. Saving my battery!
We’re home. The fog is too thick to go on tonight. Come in and get warm.

cliffhanger.text: Fog covers the top of the hill. They shelter in Nana’s house — where something is glowing…

L1-S18.sessionTitle: Make It Yours: A Helper for My Home
L1-S18.title: Nana’s Foggy Night

previously.text: The robot lit up the dark tunnel. Fog covered the hill, and they sheltered at Nana’s house…

scenes.setting: Nana Lucía’s cosy house: a kitchen, a living room with an armchair, a hallway. Fog presses at the windows.
scenes.action: Nana sits down slowly; her knees are tired after the long day. Amara brings her tea, but her hands are full.

lines.text: Oof. My knees have walked a long way today.
A robot could help at home! Carry things. Light the hallway at night.
The best robots help people where they live — kindly and safely.

scenes.setting: The toolbox on the kitchen table: pen, scoop, headlight.
scenes.action: Spark holds up each tool and imagines a home job for it: a scoop carrying a tea biscuit, a light guiding the way to bed, a pen drawing a "welcome home" path.

lines.text: Which job will your robot do? Which tool will you choose?
Ask first: what does the person need? Then choose the tool.

scenes.setting: Nana’s living room after the children’s helpers have run (plays after sharing).
scenes.action: One helper rolls under the sofa to fetch Nana’s slipper — and pushes out a glowing ball: the ninth light! Counter: 9 of 12. Outside, the fog is even thicker.

lines.text: Nine! It rolled in under the door during the storm!
Three more. But the fog is so thick, even the headlight can’t help — the light just bounces off the fog.
When you can’t see… you can still feel your way.

cliffhanger.text: Nine lights! But the fog is so thick that seeing is no help. How can a robot find its way by touch?

previously.text: They sheltered at Nana’s house. Nine lights found — but fog covered the whole hill…

scenes.setting: Morning at Nana Lucía’s house at the top of the hill. Thick white fog outside every window.
scenes.action: Amara opens the door: she can barely see her own hand. Spark switches on the robot’s headlight — the beam just makes the fog glow white.

lines.text: I can’t see anything! Not the clock, not the garden.
The light bounces off the fog, right back at us. Seeing is no help today.

scenes.setting: Inside. Nana Lucía closes her eyes and walks across the room with one hand out, touching the wall.
scenes.action: She reaches the door frame by touch. The children copy her, giggling, hands out.

lines.text: When I can’t see, I feel my way. My hand tells me: wall!
Your robot can feel too — with a bumper.

scenes.setting: Close-up of the robot. A soft foam strip clicks onto its front. Inside, a tiny switch.
scenes.action: Spark presses the foam with one finger: “click!” A little light flashes on the robot.

lines.text: Touch the bumper… click! Now your robot knows: I touched something!
That is a sensor. A sensor helps a robot feel or see the world.

scenes.setting: The foggy garden path. The garden wall is somewhere ahead — nobody knows how far.
scenes.action: Amara counts hops: “three hops!” The robot stops in the middle of nowhere. She tries five: it bumps hard. Spark shakes his head.

lines.text: I don’t know how far the wall is. How many hops?
You don’t need to know! Tell your robot: keep going until you feel a bump.
Going… going… click! Found the wall!

scenes.setting: Along the garden wall to the gate.
scenes.action: The robot feels its way: forward to the wall, a little back, turn, forward to the corner. In the corner, half hidden in the ivy, something glows warm and yellow.

lines.text: Light number ten! It was in the ivy by the gate!
Woof!
lines.direction: Bolt runs off into the fog, chasing a sound.

lines.text: Bolt! Come back!

cliffhanger.text: Ten lights! But Bolt has run off into the foggy hedge maze. How will the robot find him when it cannot see the paths?

previously.text: The robot learned to feel with a bumper. Ten lights! But Bolt ran into the foggy maze…

scenes.setting: The foggy hedge maze behind Nana’s garden. Tall green hedges, white fog.
scenes.action: From somewhere deep inside: “Woof! Woof!” Amara peers in.

lines.text: Bolt is somewhere in the maze. I can’t see the paths!
We could count hops… but we don’t have a map of this maze.

scenes.setting: At the maze entrance. Nana Lucía puts one hand on the right-hand hedge.
scenes.action: She walks slowly. Each time she meets a hedge in front, she turns right. A dotted line shows her path winding inward.

lines.text: In this maze, I have one rule. If I bump into a hedge… I turn right.
I don’t need the map. I just need my rule.

scenes.setting: A big glowing “IF” sign floats over the robot, like a road sign.
scenes.action: Two paths split from the sign: one where the bumper clicks (the robot backs off and turns), one where nothing touches (the robot keeps going).

lines.text: If is a choice. IF I feel a bump, I back off and turn right.
If I don’t feel a bump, I just keep creeping on.
Sense. Think. Act! The “if” is the thinking part!
lines.direction: Pause: let children say “Sense, think, act!”.

scenes.setting: Inside the maze, robot’s-eye view: hedge, fog, hedge.
scenes.action: The robot creeps, bumps, backs off, turns, creeps. Bolt’s barks get louder. In the middle sits Bolt, wagging, next to a glowing puddle of fog.

lines.text: Bump. Turn. Bump. Turn… Found you, Bolt!
Beep-woof!

scenes.setting: Edge of the maze. Faint music drifts up the hill. Through the fog, a pale glow above the bandstand in the town square.
scenes.action: Something on the bandstand roof flickers — then a ringing sound: “ting… ting…”.

lines.text: Listen! Something is ringing on the bandstand.
I hear it — but in this fog I can’t see how far away it is.

cliffhanger.text: Something glows and rings on the bandstand in the fog. Can a robot “hear” how far away things are?

titleCard.text: Episode 21. The Bell in the Fog.

previously.text: Bolt was found with one clever rule. Then they heard a bell ringing in the fog…

scenes.setting: Dusk on the foggy hillside. Bats flit between the trees.
scenes.action: A bat flies straight at a tree and swerves at the last moment. Close-up: little rings of sound leave the bat and bounce back from the tree.

lines.text: How do bats not crash? It’s dark AND foggy!
They shout a tiny squeak — too high for us to hear — and listen for the echo.
A quick echo means: something is close!

scenes.setting: Nana’s toolbox. A pair of round “eyes” that are really a tiny speaker and a tiny microphone.
scenes.action: The Face Screen clicks off and goes into the toolbox. The Distance Eyes click on. Rings of sound pulse out and bounce back.

lines.text: Distance Eyes! One sends a sound. One listens for the echo.
Fog can hide light. But sound goes right through it.

scenes.setting: Amara stands in front of the robot and slowly steps closer.
scenes.action: A number above the robot shrinks: 80… 50… 20. At 20, the robot’s eyes glow amber.

lines.text: The bumper feels a touch. Distance Eyes know BEFORE the touch.
Which is better for not bumping into a friend?

scenes.setting: The town square in fog. The bandstand is a dim shape; something rings on its steps: “ting… ting…”.
scenes.action: The robot rolls forward and stops just before the bandstand steps — no bump. It turns, rolls, stops again. On the top step sits a little bell with a glowing light caught inside its handle.

lines.text: Something is close. Stopping!
Light eleven! It was ringing the bell every time the wind blew.

scenes.setting: The square fills with the shapes of people setting up stalls for tonight. Bolt dashes between their legs.
scenes.action: A delivery cart rolls by; someone steps out right in front of the robot. Everyone freezes.

lines.text: Careful! The square is full of people today — and so many children!
A robot in a crowd has a very big job: keep everyone safe.

cliffhanger.text: Eleven lights! The square is filling with people for tonight’s festival. How can a robot move safely in a crowd?

previously.text: Distance Eyes found light eleven by its echo. The square filled with people for the festival…

scenes.setting: The town square on festival day. The fog is lifting. Stalls, garlands, a juggler, children running.
scenes.action: The robot has to carry the eleventh light to the clock tower door across the square. People cross in front of it again and again.

lines.text: There are people everywhere! How do we get across?
A good robot never rushes through people. It waits.

scenes.setting: A zebra crossing at the edge of the square. Noor, the little girl from the bakery street, holds her father’s hand.
scenes.action: They stop, look, wait for a cart to pass, then cross. Spark copies them.

lines.text: We stop. We look. We wait. Then we go!
Your robot can do that too. Before each hop: wait until the path is clear.

scenes.setting: Robot’s-eye view: the distance number above the robot.
scenes.action: A juggler steps in front: the number drops to 30 and the robot waits. He steps away: the number jumps to 150, and the robot hops.

lines.text: Path not clear. Waiting… Clear! Hop!
It waited for the juggler! Good robot!

scenes.setting: Nana Lucía sits on a bench with the children.
scenes.action: She shows an old photo: young Lucía in a workshop with a big robot arm behind a yellow safety fence.

lines.text: When I built robots, the first question was always: how do we keep people safe?
Who keeps a robot safe? The robot?
The people who build it and program it. That’s you now.

scenes.setting: The clock tower door. It creaks open onto a dark ramp spiralling up inside the tower.
scenes.action: Far above, a faint glow and a soft “tick… tock…”. The ramp disappears round a corner.

lines.text: The last light must be at the top of the tower!
The ramp goes round and round. And it’s a hill — hops get shorter on a hill.

cliffhanger.text: The twelfth light is at the top of the clock tower, up a winding ramp. Counting hops on a hill went wrong before. What will work?

titleCard.text: Episode 23. The Top of the Tower.

previously.text: The robot waited for people in the busy square. The last light was at the top of the clock tower…

scenes.setting: Inside the clock tower: a ramp that winds up around the walls, corner after corner. Big brass gears turn slowly.
scenes.action: Amara counts hops on the first ramp. The robot stops short — the ramp is a hill.

lines.text: Three hops… but it stopped too early! Just like the iron lantern hill.
On a hill, each hop is shorter. Counting goes wrong. What never goes wrong?
The Distance Eyes! Go until the wall is close!

scenes.setting: Ramp after ramp, from above.
scenes.action: The robot goes until close, turns left, goes until close, turns left. Spark counts the corners on his fingers: one, two, three, four.

lines.text: Go until close. Turn. Go until close. Turn. It’s a pattern!
Four times. Repeat!

scenes.setting: Halfway up, a window looks out over Lantern Hill. Nana Lucía rests on a step.
scenes.action: Picture-in-picture: real-looking scenes of people working with robots — an engineer at a drawing table, a technician fixing a robot arm, a programmer at a laptop, a doctor beside a hospital delivery robot, a farmer with a fruit-picking robot.

lines.text: Lots of people work with robots. Some draw the plans. Some build them. Some write programs.
Some test them, and some fix them when they break.
I’ve done ALL of those this year!

scenes.setting: The top of the tower, inside the great clock face. Twelve empty round holders in a circle.
scenes.action: In the middle of the gears sits the twelfth light, stuck in a cog. The robot stops just in front, the scoop gently lifts it free.

lines.text: Twelve! We found all twelve!
Beep-woof! Woof!

scenes.setting: Looking out from the clock face at sunset. Below, the whole town is getting ready for the Night of a Hundred Lights.
scenes.action: Eleven lights in a basket, one in the scoop. Nana Lucía puts a hand on the child’s robot.

lines.text: Tonight is the festival. The town will want a show from the robot that brought the lights home.
A show that YOU design!

cliffhanger.text: All twelve lights are found! Tonight is the Night of a Hundred Lights — and the town wants a show from your robot.

L1-S24.sessionTitle: Make It Yours: The Night of a Hundred Lights
L1-S24.title: The Night of a Hundred Lights

titleCard.text: Episode 24. The Night of a Hundred Lights.

previously.text: All twelve lights were found at the top of the clock tower. Tonight is the festival…

scenes.setting: Evening. The town square, the clock tower above it. Families with paper lanterns. Everyone from the season is there: Mr Okafor, Noor, Ms Mei, Mr Diego, Ms Adaeze, Mr Haruto, Captain Ingrid.
scenes.action: The twelve lights are put back one by one into the clock. Each one glows as it clicks in. The crowd counts with them.

lines.text: One, two, three… ten, eleven… twelve!
The Lantern Clock shines again!

scenes.setting: A stage area in the square, marked with a festival mat.
scenes.action: Spark flies to the middle with a tiny microphone. Amara holds up a planning sheet with drawings and arrows.

lines.text: And now — a robot show! Designed by YOU.
Plan it first. Then build it, test it, fix it — and show everyone!
Use what you have learned: a loop, a sensor, a tool, and kind words.

scenes.setting: The same square, after the children’s shows. This scene and the next play at the certificate moment — straight after sharing, or in a separate short slot (see the teacher notes).
scenes.action: Fireworks of light from the clock. Nana Lucía holds up a scroll tied with ribbon: the certificate. Bolt wears a tiny lantern on his collar.

lines.text: You built a robot. You taught it to move, to draw, to carry, to feel and to listen. And you kept everyone safe.
When your Explorer badges are all done, this scroll has your name on it. You are a real Robot Explorer.
Thank you for bringing the lights home!

scenes.setting: Late night. Everyone has gone home. A paper boat drifts into the harbour carrying a sealed glass bottle.
scenes.action: Amara pulls out a map of islands across the sea, and a message: “Our island needs a robot builder. Come soon.”

lines.text: A map of islands! And a message for us!
A new adventure… for when you’re ready.

cliffhanger.text: A bottle washes into the harbour with a map of islands across the sea: “Our island needs a robot builder.” (Level 2 begins here.)
